claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films are single-phase and hexagonal.
The as-deposited films exhibit a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have relatively high defect densities and residual lattice strains.
Higher defect densities and residual lattice strains mediate the abrupt and hysteretic magnetocaloric response of the as-deposited films.
Post-deposition annealing below the magnetostructural, order-disorder, and recrystallization thresholds can promote defect recovery while avoiding major structural changes.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will reduce microstructural defects in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will relieve residual lattice strains in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Grain boundaries, dislocations, and other microstructural defects influence nucleation and growth of the magnetostructural phase.
Defect recovery and lattice-strain relief produce a more homogeneous distribution of nucleation sites.
Defect recovery and lattice-strain relief lower the nucleation barrier for the magnetostructural transition.
A lower nucleation barrier promotes a more gradual magnetostructural phase transformation.
Annealed films will have a broader transition-temperature range than as-deposited films.
Annealed films will exhibit a smoother, less abrupt entropy-change profile than as-deposited films.
Annealed films will exhibit reduced thermal or magnetic hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealing may moderately reduce or shift the peak magnetocaloric effect.
The predictions apply to deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films with moderate initial defect densities and a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The predictions apply under low-applied-field cycling near the transition temperature, provided that annealing does not form secondary phases.
The magnitude of hysteresis reduction and transition broadening depends on composition and annealing parameters.
